page: Microsoft Azure M176bds_4_v3 is a memory-optimized cloud server built for data-intensive enterprise workloads requiring extreme memory capacity. Powered by the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor on the x86_64 architecture, the instance utilizes an Intel Xeon 8473C processor operating at frequencies up to 4.0 GHz. The configuration allocates 176 dedicated vCPUs backed by 88 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The CPU subsystem includes 48 KB of L1 data cache per core, 2 MB of L2 cache per core, and a shared 105 MB L3 cache, complemented by Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and AVX-512 vector support. System memory totals 3,892.0 GB, yielding a high density of approximately 22.11 GB of RAM per vCPU. The server bundles 8,590 GB of local solid-state drive (SSD) storage, contains zero discrete GPUs, and provides no complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations highlight exceptional throughput in memory-bound and parallel execution scenarios. Multi-core CPU evaluations under stress-ng and PassMark place the instance in the top tier, matching its high core count. The memory subsystem delivers uncached read bandwidth of 432.05 GB/sec and write bandwidth of 186.0 GB/sec on large 256 MB blocks, driving top-tier rankings in Redis SET operations and PassMark database operations tests. Parallelized compression benchmarks such as multi-threaded bzip3 decompression also attain top-tier classifications, while CPU-driven large-model LLM prompt processing achieves strong performance using available vector and matrix extensions. Conversely, single-threaded metrics, including stress-ng single-core and bzip3 single-core decompression, test within average tiers, reflecting typical per-thread limits of high-density multi-socket architectures.

From an infrastructure efficiency perspective, the M176bds_4_v3 consolidates substantial memory and local NVMe-equivalent SSD capacity into a single node, reducing the network overhead and serialization latency associated with distributed caching tiers. The trade-off centers on its architectural imbalance for purely compute-bound or single-threaded tasks, which do not leverage the vast RAM allocation. Consequently, the instance is appropriate for massive in-memory databases such as SAP HANA, Redis, and memcached clusters, large-scale transaction processing systems, high-volume extract-transform-load (ETL) pipelines, and memory-constrained analytical data warehouses.
description: Microsoft Azure M176bds_4_v3 is a memory-optimized instance engineered for large-scale enterprise data workloads. Built on the x86_64 Intel Xeon 8473C processor running up to 4.0 GHz, it provides 176 dedicated vCPUs across 88 physical cores, a 105 MB L3 cache, and Intel AMX hardware matrix acceleration. The architecture pairs 3,892.0 GB of system memory, delivering roughly 22.11 GB per vCPU, with 8,590 GB of bundled local SSD storage and no integrated GPUs. Multi-core throughput and memory operations rank in the top tier across synthetic and database benchmarks, including Redis transactions, PassMark database execution, and uncached read bandwidth. While single-threaded processing scores in the average tier, its extreme memory density and high core allocation make it technically suited for massive in-memory databases, large data warehousing, extensive analytical processing, and CPU-based LLM inference.
